$comment: Every rendered verdict AND every rendered measurement on this page carries a marker, and every marker listed here has been forced false and watched go red. A mutation counts only when the unmutated baseline passed in the same session, the failure was that marker's OWN assertion, and the run served the mutated bundle (CI=1, port 4684, no reused server). e2e/verdicts.spec.ts fails on any rendered marker missing from this file, on any marker here the page no longer renders, and on any mutation whose killedBy test does not assert the marker through expectVerdict/expectClaim -- a text-only assertion says nothing about state and cannot be recorded as a kill. Every branch that writes a marker has its own mutation: markers with more than one code path carry more than one entry, because covering the marker is not the same as covering the branch.

dleq.renders: #dleq — whether the client accepted the issuer's DLEQ proof under the key it was told to trust

killedBy.test: an unpublished issuer key aborts issuance, and the token a careless client keeps is refused

mutations.kills: expectVerdict(page, 'dleq', { text: 'DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED', result: 'good' })
mutations.observed: baseline 16 passed in the same session, unmutated tree md5 src/main.ts f1345c0c3d45c44b1fb0137cefe1caa1, src/pass/privacy-pass.ts b62b91b22af8364862277861d4b5ffb4, src/oprf/voprf.ts 142a1828adbfff02fc9984b4e6dd8a9b; mutated 3a8bc6fd7a4a3b455891ee6a104de616 1 failed / 15 passed. Verbatim: "Error: verdict "dleq" text / expect(locator).toContainText(expected) failed / Locator: locator('[data-verdict="dleq"]') / Expected substring: "DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED" / Received string: "DLEQ PROOF · ACCEPTED AN UNPUBLISHED KEY"" at e2e/claims.spec.ts in "an unpublished issuer key aborts issuance, and the token a careless client keeps is refused". The client stopped refusing the unpublished key and finalized a token against it. `return true` alone does not build here -- tsconfig sets noUnusedLocals, so the composites go unused and `tsc -b` fails the webServer before a single test runs. A build failure is not a kill; the mutation is `|| true` on the same return, which leaves every value used and still makes the verifier accept everything.

mutations.kills: expectVerdict(page, 'dleq', { text: 'DLEQ PROOFS · BOTH VERIFIED', result: 'good' })
mutations.observed: baseline 16 passed in the same session, unmutated tree md5 src/main.ts f1345c0c3d45c44b1fb0137cefe1caa1, src/pass/privacy-pass.ts b62b91b22af8364862277861d4b5ffb4, src/oprf/voprf.ts 142a1828adbfff02fc9984b4e6dd8a9b; mutated d5cf5718342642e7b25e41ea53cf66a5 2 failed / 14 passed. Verbatim: "Error: verdict "dleq" text / Expected substring: "DLEQ PROOFS · BOTH VERIFIED" / Received string: "DLEQ PROOF · REJECTED AS DESIGNED"" at e2e/claims.spec.ts in "valid proofs under client-specific keys redeem and reveal partitioning". M1 could not reach this path -- it forces DLEQ verification to accept, which leaves BOTH VERIFIED standing. The second failure is collateral, not a second finding: e2e/a11y.spec.ts:31 walks the partition fixture and clicks "2. Redeem at origin" unconditionally, and the abort leaves that button disabled, so it times out.

This is the mutation the old harness could not see. It leaves the map's drawn lines and every word on the page untouched and changes only the state the marker publishes, so a toContainText kill would have SURVIVED it. The shared helper asserts text, data-result and palette as one claim, and the attribute is what went red.
